reviews.text: Skilfully adapted for the screen from her 2015 novel of the same name, Jessica Knoll has brought contemporary concerns alive in a harrowingly thrilling film.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: This movie just doesn't quite work...It felt like a very fashionable Hallmark movie.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive is able to tie everything up with a neat bow at the end because nothing was ever unpacked to begin with. This latest Netflix Original is sensationalized trauma packaged neatly for the true-crime-obsessed crowd.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Some tighter editing, a deeper script and short run-time would've worked in the movies favour, but what we were delivered was a tough yet enjoyable watch that does what it says on the tin.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Much of the film almost comes across as a forgettable CW drama. ... [Mila] Kunis is certainly a talented actress, but the material for this film was simply not endearing enough to make it memorable for its audience.
reviews.author: Richard Schertzer

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive delivers a heartbreakingly real feeling story about just how coldly the world can be to someone who has survived traumatic events.
reviews.author: Charles Hartford

reviews.text: Seen as a clarifying film about the silences that usually surround abuse or as a shooter elegy –whichever it is, affirmative capitalism is the one that ends up triumphant– what remains of Luckiest girl alive is the idea of ​​something uncomfortably bland.
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: Mila Kunis is good but not good enough to make this movie anything better than average entertainment.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: there’s a decent film in here somewhere about trauma’s ripple effects and people’s coping mechanisms. ... [But] As a thriller, the jolts just aren’t there, and ginning up those elements saps Ani’s journey of emotional weight.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive throws a miniseries worth of ideas into a lacklustre movie.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Messily (and almost irresponsibly) waffles between tones, and would perhaps have benefited from embracing the black comedy genre it dives into at first... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Milagros Amondaray

reviews.text: It all adds up. But the result isn't always more, sometimes it adds up to less. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: For Kunis, “Luckiest Girl Alive” marks her career acting zenith. In her performance that’s not all that far removed from her Oscar-nominated turn in the equally unnerving “The Black Swan,” Kunis never attempts to soften or sand-down Ani’s rougher edges.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: The film has a somewhat discursive start before coming together to deliver a very potent second half.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Some of the sequences are difficult to watch at times. But with great storytelling and exceptional performances from both Kunis and Aurelia, it is definitely a film worth watching.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: Sometimes irritatingly confusing and redundant.  Yet it remains engrossing and, in the end, compelling, even if the way it wraps things up is rather obvious and self-congratulatory.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: After a chaotic opening stanza, Luckiest Girl Alive has plenty going for it.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: These are important issues and, even if the narrative is drawn out, director Mike Barker's approach has both gripping tension and resonant commentary that deserves to strike a nerve.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: This emotionally taxing film is likely to spark debate about the portrayal of both sexual and school violence and its repercussions, and Kunis' compelling lead performance drives that portrayal.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Amidst the rash of films using school shootings as a plot driver, this shameful exploitation of it doubles down with another horrific personal trauma all so its lead character can finally learn how to write something meaningful for the New York Times
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: In a nutshell, Luckiest Girl Alive lacks the gravitas it deserves. At least Amy, the Gone Girl antagonist, was a fascinating psychopath. But, there is no subtext here, only surface and trauma that fails to engage.
reviews.author: Archika Khurana

reviews.text: The issue here is how the story is told... just because the movie tells us an important, inherently powerful, story doesn't make the movie good. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The issues here couldn’t be more pertinent. But Knoll’s thriller is a sleek but pretty crude example of processing PTSD for Netflix and chilling...
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: At times unsettling, others a bit crass, clumsy, and even chaotic, but, where the film fails, Mila Kunis rescues it from being totally ridiculous and absurd. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Even when Luckiest Girl Alive doesn't manage to sell its plot contrivances all the time, Kunis' breathtaking performance manages to make us buy some of it.
reviews.author: Poulomi Das

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive keeps telling us that we are watching a biting depiction of sublimated grief and rage, but the movie bounces along at such a weird pace that nothing can sink in or register as more than garish, tossed-off plot detail.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Though it’s not the most thrilling or suspenseful movie, it achieves its goal of showing a character reconcile the horrific events in her past and get revenge on those who wronged her.
reviews.author: Marissa Crenwelge

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive is watchable only because of Mila Kunis, who does a stellar job of fleshing out her character.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: The film never rises to exceptional heights with its visuals and doesn’t quite have the moving writing Knoll was praised for when she wrote her book.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: From its very title, Luckiest Girl Alive sends a message that not only bears repeating but demands it.
reviews.author: Erick Massoto

reviews.text: As formulaic as it is, the story nonetheless confronts the persistence of guilt over past questionable behavior and how people struggle to deal with it, even long after the fact.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive falls short of its promise, a reminder that, however ironic the title is intended to be, fortune tends to favor the bold.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Well written, but difficult to watch...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Small edits could have propelled the film into a dark drama instead of something resembling a PSA.
reviews.author: Samantha Bergeson

reviews.text: As a book, Luckiest Girl Alive was frequently compared to Gone Girl. The same isn’t likely to happen with the movie version, evidencing the difference a strong adaptation and director can make.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Kunis’s alpha female appears at once ferocious and like a conspicuous sham. (Imagine Sheryl Sandberg as a “Scooby-Doo” villain.)
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Falls into the trap of trying too hard to capture not just the book’s flashback-heavy plot but also its distinctive voice.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive can be tonally haphazard and occasionally – beware: P-word impending – problematic, but it’s also frequently gripping, and rendered empathetic by an inspired Kunis.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: While it's a fascinating character piece, there's no breathing room to fully explore the film’s many storylines. A miniseries would have been more effective in adapting a novel that touches on many important subjects that need the appropriate rumination.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Visceral while also empowering, Luckiest Girl Alive holds the viewer’s attention with an absorbing mystery and moments of sobering reality.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: It's a film held aloft by a terrific cast and some truly potent elements in the writing, but stifled by a paucity of bigger picture thinking.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: This film leaves nothing to the imagination, and its star, Kunis, is easily the best part of the entire movie.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: [Exploits] both school shootings and rape trauma for a self-actualization narrative that ultimately ends with Ani finding value not in the release of her repressed emotions through this writing, but in the shallow achievement of viral fame.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Girl isn't a great movie or even a good one, really, but it has Kunis kicking her stiletto through a taxi-cab window and quoting William Faulkner, and it's right there in your queue.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It’s clear what Barker was attempting to achieve... a Gone Girl-like tale of revenge about sexual assault. But, sadly, the film lacks the depth and catharsis required to live up to such a thought-provoking predecessor.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive revolves around a narrative choice so dumbfounding and of such dubious taste that all of the movie's intentions have to be re-assessed.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: No one, especially not the viewer, is lucky.
reviews.author: Amy Amatangelo

reviews.text: The story it ultimately tells is an empty, self-serving fantasy.
reviews.author: Adrian Horton

reviews.text: It’s up to Kunis to carry the film, and for the most part she does.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A distant, atonal film that feels more slippery than evocative.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: Kunis is a better actress here than anyone has ever asked her to be. (Maybe after this, people will start asking.)
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Some may see it all as “shock value” and nothing more (especially since the film’s resolution is relatively rudimentary and redundant for a story like this).
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Utilizing a traditionally glossy, chick-lit-retrofitted heroine as a mouthpiece for somber, serious activist sentiments isn’t so much provocative as just downright batty.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive is a misguided Me Too tale that quickly goes off the rails and has no sense or sensitivity whatsoever in what it chooses to depict on-screen
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Luckiest Girl Alive focuses on very difficult subject matters but the film handles it with the right tone and care.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: From Jessica Knoll's screenplay to Mike Barker's direction, the film fails its actors and audience, delving more into trauma porn than a sensitively handled mystery.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

synopsis: Luckiest Girl Alive centers on Ani FaNelli, a sharp-tongued New Yorker who appears to have it all: a sought-after position at a glossy magazine, a killer wardrobe, and a dream Nantucket wedding on the horizon. But when the director of a crime documentary invites her to tell her side of the shocking incident that took place when she was a teenager at the prestigious Brentley School, Ani is forced to confront a dark truth that threatens to unravel her meticulously crafted life.
